rationale: bugs_open/215: WriteSitePlanAction canonicalises each emitted page independently and then inserts one row per entry, with nothing deduplicating the list in between. Both destination tables are uniquely indexed on that canonical name (site_plan_pages UNIQUE(plan_id,name); site_plan_sections UNIQUE(plan_id,page_name,ordering)), and the write is a single transaction, so the moment the planner LLM emits one page under two spellings the ENTIRE replan is lost with SQLSTATE 23505 — an error naming neither the canonicaliser nor the LLM, whose likeliest wrong reading is a stale index or a concurrent write. Live incident 2026-08-08 on fundamentallyai (corr 1cb17b11-fd10-4d52-836c-36e2fa246ff6). The same dual-identity defect also has a quiet mode that reached production: the 2026-08-07 replan of the same site created three page rows that were canonical/stem twins of pages already serving under the other spelling — permanent 404s, active from creation and therefore valid internal-link targets, which another front had to hand-archive along with four work items pointing at them. This fix closes the crash door at the only place that writes these tables, so the collision becomes unrepresentable whatever the LLM emits. It is a contained bug fix inside one action: no new shared vocabulary, no new contract, no new capability reachable by any other pipeline — the sole additive surface is one integer key in the action's own returned map, and nothing in Go or in live config reads any key of that map (measured, see grounded_in). I am NOT claiming an ordering constraint: HEAD is shared and any session's build ships this, per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29.

plan.summary: Collapse post-canonicalisation duplicate pages inside WriteSitePlanAction before any insert. New pure helper dedupePlanPageRows keeps one row per canonical name in first-appearance order; the entry with more sections wins (a zero-section stub loses to a composed page), ties keep the first, and blank optional metadata on the winner is backfilled from the loser (fills a blank, never overwrites). Every merge is logged naming both raw spellings, and the discarded section list is logged at Warn whenever authored content is actually dropped. The function-local planPageRow type is hoisted to package scope (plus a non-persisted RawName field) so the helper is unit-testable without a database. Seven tests, including one that pins the canonicaliser's collapse behaviour so this cannot rot into dead code.

edits.rationale: The type was declared inside WriteSitePlanAction, which forced any dedup logic to live inline in a function that needs a live *sql.DB and a transaction — i.e. untestable without a database. Hoisting it to package scope is what makes the fix a pure, unit-tested function rather than more untested code inside the transaction body. RawName carries the LLM's own spelling; it is written to no column and exists solely so a merge log line can name the two entries that collided, which is the only thing that makes a collision diagnosable after the run's orchestration row expires (measured at 24h for failures).

edits.rationale: The fix itself, and the only door: this is the sole writer of site_plan_pages/site_plan_sections from a planner emission, so collapsing here makes a duplicate canonical name unrepresentable downstream rather than merely less likely. Merge rule chosen to discard the least: more sections wins (the observed shape is one composed page plus one zero-section stub, and the stub carries nothing), tie keeps first so the rule is total and order-stable. The Warn branch REPORTS a lossy merge, it does not decide one — an earlier draft let it force first-wins and thereby discarded the richer page; that defect was caught by its own test and is now pinned by TestDedupePlanPageRows_RicherComposedWinsEvenWhenSecond. Metadata backfill is guarded to blank fields only, so it can never overwrite an authored value.

Wire the helper in at the only correct point: after canonicalisation (the step that creates the collision) and before the transaction opens, so no insert can ever see a duplicate name. Placed after the existing empty-plan guard so that guard keeps its current meaning. The aggregate Warn fires only when a collision actually occurred, so a healthy plan write is byte-identical in behaviour and log output to today.

Durable observability, and it exists because the bug file's own stated verification cannot work. That verification was 'after the fix ships, re-run the census for SQLSTATE 23505 on idx_site_plan_pages_name in orchestration_states.error'. Measured today: every FAILED row in that table is under 24 hours old (0 older), so for a low-frequency emission-variance event that census reads 0 both before and after the fix — it could not come out otherwise, and would have looked like proof. A counter on the action's own result, plus the log lines, is a signal that can actually be non-zero. Additive only: nothing in Go and no live agent config reads any key of this map (measured).

Two layers on purpose. The first test pins the PREMISE — that distinct descriptors really do canonicalise to one name — across all three collapse families (tool/guide/game prefix, homepage, section-index), so that if the canonicaliser ever stops collapsing, the suite says the dedup has become dead code instead of leaving it silently inert. The rest cover the fix: the live incident's exact stub-vs-composed shape with the stub emitted FIRST (so 'keep first' alone cannot pass), the tie, the richer-second case that caught a real defect mid-build, blank-only metadata backfill, a three-way collision, and the property the indexes actually require (no duplicate name survives). One test asserts the NO-OP case: a plan with no collisions passes through with order and membership untouched. All three guards were mutation-tested — disabling the dedup fails 6 of 7; forcing keep-first fails; unguarding the backfill fails.

grounded_in: The failure, quoted from the live run (corr 1cb17b11-fd10-4d52-836c-36e2fa246ff6, fundamentallyai, 2026-08-08): 'step write_site_plan failed: ... insert site_plan_pages for "tool-llm-cost-calculator": ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_site_plan_pages_name" (SQLSTATE 23505)'. The insert names r.Name, so two rows in planRows carried that canonical name.

No dedup exists on the path, re-read at HEAD 2026-08-09: the canonicalise loop appends unconditionally (write_site_plan_action.go:276-315) and the insert loop executes one statement per row (:355-381, pre-edit numbering).

TWO crash doors, not one — read from the live schema today, and the second is not in the bug file: 'idx_site_plan_pages_name' UNIQUE, btree (plan_id, name) on site_plan_pages; 'idx_site_plan_sections_key' UNIQUE, btree (plan_id, page_name, ordering) on site_plan_sections. A duplicate name aborts at the pages insert first, so the sections index has never been the observed error — but it is a second door onto the same state and the same fix closes both. There is NO unique index on url, so a URL collision is not a third door (checked, negative).

The collision generator, read at HEAD in datahelpers/page_canonical.go rather than inferred from the incident: role 'tool' does bare := strings.TrimPrefix(slug, "tool-") then returns "tool-"+bare (:153-162), so slug 'x' and slug 'tool-x' both produce 'tool-x'; guide (:164-173) and game (:175-184) are identical in shape. Role 'index' returns ('index','/index.html','landing') (:117-119) and slug 'home'/'index' under empty/content/landing does the same (:125-127), so a plan naming both a homepage and a 'home' page collides. isSectionIndexRole trims a '-index' suffix and re-adds it (:136-149), so slug 'guides' and slug 'guides-index' both produce 'guides-index'. That is THREE collision families; the bug file names only the first, and the homepage family is the likeliest of the three in ordinary emission.

The quiet mode is measured, not argued: the 2026-08-07 replan of fundamentallyai wrote three rows created 08-07 08:24:22, all status planned + deployed_at IS NULL + zero components, each a canonical/stem twin of a page already serving 200 under the other spelling (tool-llm-cost-calculator vs llm-cost-calculator; tool-tools vs tools; ai-readiness-checker-guide vs tool-ai-readiness-checker-guide). Note the direction flips — the phantom is the canonical form twice and the stem form once — so the invariant is two identities for one page, not a fixed prefix. Hand-archived by another front on 08-08 along with four work items pointing at them.

Blast radius of the new returned key, measured rather than asserted: grep for pages_written/sections_written/duplicate_pages_merged across all non-test Go returns zero consumers; and in live config, SELECT over active non-snapshot agent_definitions for 'pages_written' or 'sections_written' returns zero rows. The only definition referencing write_site_plan at all is build-site-planner (the step declaration itself). So the added key is inert to every consumer that exists today.

Why the bug file's stated verification cannot work, and why this submission adds a counter instead: SELECT status, count(*), min(created_at) FROM orchestration_states GROUP BY status shows FAILED rows spanning 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-09 only, and 'failed rows older than 24h' counts 0 against 4,935 rows total (oldest row overall 2026-07-13, so the table itself is not 24h-limited — the failures are). The census for error LIKE '%idx_site_plan_pages_name%' returns 0 today, and the 2026-08-08 incident IS one of these, so 0 measures the retention window, not the frequency. It would read 0 after the fix regardless of whether the fix worked.

The no-op case is tested, not assumed: TestDedupePlanPageRows_PreservesOrderAndDistinctPages asserts that a four-page plan with no collisions comes out with identical membership, identical order, and merges == 0 — so the common path is unchanged. Package result: go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/ passes in the working tree AND at clean HEAD via git archive (both 'ok'), so this adds no failure and masks none.

Mutation evidence that the guards are load-bearing (each mutation applied to a copy, run, reverted): making dedupePlanPageRows a pass-through fails 6 of 7 tests, with only the no-op order test still passing as it must; replacing the section-count comparison with 'if false' (always keep first) fails; replacing the backfill guard 'if winner.Title == ""' with 'if true' fails.

Relation to this front's own work (bugs_open/151 candidate 1): fact assignments ride inside each page's section entries, so the merge preserves the winner's assigned_fact_ids intact by construction — the survivor's Sections slice is carried whole, never merged element-wise. A collision today loses the entire replan including all assignments, so this fix is also a precondition for any clean compliance observation on that front.
plan.risks: Three things I would most like checked, in order. (1) The merge rule discards a section list in one branch — when both colliding entries are composed. I chose 'richer wins, tie keeps first' over the bug file's original 'keep first' because it discards strictly less in every case, but it IS a silent content loss at Warn level rather than a hard failure; the alternative of failing the write on an ambiguous collision would preserve today's data-loss-free-but-plan-lost behaviour for that sub-case. I think logging and proceeding is right — losing the whole replan is the worse outcome and is what the bug is — but it is a judgement, not a measurement. (2) Metadata backfill from the discarded entry: guarded to blank-only so it cannot overwrite authored text, but it does mean a stub's title can reach a page the stub did not compose. Reviewers may reasonably prefer no backfill at all; it is three lines to drop and one test to delete. (3) Scope: I have treated this as a contained bug fix, not a platform seam, on the grounds that it adds no shared vocabulary, no contract and no capability any other pipeline can reach — the one additive surface is an integer in this action's own result map with zero measured consumers. If the guardian seat reads the merge SEMANTICS as a shared guarantee (i.e. 'the plan writer may now silently drop an emitted page'), that is a scope call I would rather have made explicitly here than discovered after the fact, per the 2026-07-28 ruling. Not addressed by this change, deliberately and separately: the quiet mode where a plan row and an existing live page carry two identities for the same page — that needs reconciliation against realised pages under either spelling, lives in the reconciler rather than this action, and is left in bugs_open/215 rather than smuggled into a bug patch. Also unchanged: page-scope imagery scope_refs still key off the RAW LLM page name rather than the canonical one (write_site_plan_action.go flattenImageryBlock), which is bugs_open/214's territory; this fix neither improves nor worsens it, but a reviewer should know the two name-spaces coexist on this path.
